claims.text: A hierarchically nanostructured Ni-based alloy electrode can provide enhanced catalytic activity for both HER and HOR.
A hierarchically nanostructured Ni-based alloy electrode can provide prolonged durability during HER and HOR.
Partial dealloying or templated etching of a Ni-based alloy can produce a hierarchical nanostructure.
Ni-Al or Ni-Cu alloys are proposed as fully alloyed precursor substrates.
Controlled dealloying selectively removes less noble alloy components.
Controlled dealloying or templated etching creates a high-surface-area nanoporous microstructure.
The proposed processing forms interconnected pores and channels throughout the Ni-based scaffold.
The proposed processing forms catalytic nanofacets throughout the Ni-based scaffold.
The nanoporous architecture increases the density of catalytically active sites.
Abundant active sites on the nanoporous Ni-based surface improve hydrogen adsorption and desorption kinetics.
The Ni framework maintains mechanical integrity and chemical stability under aggressive electrochemical conditions.
Minor Fe or Mo additions may help maintain mechanical integrity and chemical stability.
The nanostructured electrode is predicted to exhibit lower HER and HOR onset potentials than an unstructured reference.
The nanostructured electrode is predicted to produce higher currents at fixed overpotentials than an unstructured reference.
The nanostructured electrode is predicted to have greater structural longevity than conventional Ni or similar non-nanostructured catalysts.
Performance depends on nanoporous-layer thickness and pore size.
Performance depends on the choice of minor alloying elements.
Performance under extremely corrosive conditions or high current densities has not been validated.
